To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DNA polymerase ν is able to efficiently bypass large lesions that are located in the DNA major groove, but not in the minor groove, and that it is able, albeit with reduced capability, to incorporate a nucleotide opposite (+)-trans-antibenzo[a] pyrene-7, 8-dihydrodil-9,10-oxide-dA.

pol ν is able to catalyze translesion DNA replication across exceptionally large major groove DNA−DNA and DNA−protein cross-links, and it can bypass the 1,N2-etheno-dG adduct in an error-free fashion, but it does so with greatly diminished efficiency.
pol ν is able to catalyze translesion DNA polymerization past major groove DNA−protein cross-links (DNA−peptide cross-links), and DNA interstrand DNA−DNA cross-link lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel TLS activities of pol ν and its potential roles in the bypass of large DNA lesions.
the characterization of the TLS activity of pol ν and its substrate specificity, which may provide insights into the biological functions of pol ν.
the characterization of the TLS capability of DNA polymerase ν and the identification of novel TLS substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pol ν is a TLS polymerase with a novel specificity for major groove DNA lesions and a low fidelity bypass capability for minor groove DNA lesions and DNA interstrand adducts.

the TLS capability of pol ν is not restricted to high fidelity replication bypass only of thymine lesions, but can also be extended to bypass of some major groove DNA−peptide cross-links, and DNA−DNA interstrand cross-links.
pol ν is a TLS enzyme that can bypass a variety of DNA lesions, albeit with a different spectrum of substrate specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pol ν has a unique substrate specificity in TLS, bypassing large DNA adducts with linkage to the major groove but not to the minor groove.
pol ν has a broad TLS spectrum that includes major and minor groove DNA adduct and interstrand cross-links, and it is able to replicate DNA templates containing εdA and (+)-BPDE-dG lesions.
pol ν is a versatile TLS polymerase with the capability to bypass a wide spectrum of bulky DNA adducts and cross-linking lesions, albeit with different efficiencies and error rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
POLN is capable of bypassing a broad range of bulky DNA adducts and that its bypass capacity cannot be predicted based on its substrate specificity for the DNA lesion.
POLN is able to bypass major groove DNA adduction and interstrand cross-linkage, but is blocked by minor groove DNA lesions.
pol ν is a novel TLS polymerase that is capable of bypassing a wide range of major groove DNA lesions.
